subject.title: Bug: OpenClaw 2026.4.9 exposes agent internal thinking (English) to user

question: Should maintainers authorize a narrow security-sensitive repair for the embedded streaming reasoning-tag scanner now?
rationale: The fix shape is clear, but the item is about hidden reasoning exposure to external chat recipients and already carries no-new-fix-pr plus needs-security-review labels, so automation should pause for maintainer/security approval.

options.title: Approve narrow sanitizer repair
options.body: Update the embedded streaming scanner to use the shared reasoning-tag grammar and add regression tests for attribute-bearing streamed tags; this is the recommended path.

options.title: Fold into broader sanitizer work
options.body: Keep this issue linked to broader channel-sanitizer reports, but do not close it until the exact core streaming scanner gap is fixed or explicitly absorbed.

options.title: Require live channel proof first
options.body: Ask for a packaged WeChat/weixin proof before authorizing a fix, accepting slower resolution despite the current source-level reproduction.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow sanitizer repair
recommendation.body: Update the embedded streaming scanner to use the shared reasoning-tag grammar and add regression tests for attribute-bearing streamed tags; this is the recommended path.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently carried the embedded subscription split and have prior shared reasoning-tag ownership in the relevant history.
